bank_plan.formula: (lesson_check_items + module_check_items) x 2 alternates + forms x form_length
bank_plan.eighty_twenty_note: 80% instruction / 20% assessment honoured at course level (I+A=T); bank serves lesson checks, module checks, 3 practice forms and a protected final.
bank_plan.size_band_note: Planning range per assessment standard (200-600 skills; 600-1500+ large certification). This is a planning guide, not proof of quality.

mcq_limitation_note: Knowledge-practice forms use MCQ/MR only; official item formats not reproducible in this format are listed in the exam-version record.

items.stem: In an IaaS deployment, which responsibility always remains with the customer?

options.text: Operating system patching and data protection
options.rationale: Correct: in IaaS the customer manages the OS upward, including data.
Physical security is always the provider's responsibility.
The provider maintains the virtualisation layer.
Hardware lifecycle is the provider's responsibility.

items.explanation: IaaS leaves OS, runtime and data to the customer; the provider owns the physical and virtualisation layers.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: A company must keep encryption keys outside the cloud provider's control for a sensitive dataset. Which approach fits?

options.text: Customer-managed keys held in the customer's own key service (BYOK/HYOK)
options.rationale: Correct: holding keys under customer control keeps the provider from decrypting data.
Default provider keys leave the provider able to decrypt.
Removing encryption increases exposure and fails the requirement.
Transport encryption does not protect data at rest or control keys.

items.explanation: Customer-held keys ensure the provider cannot decrypt the data.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: Which TWO controls most directly reduce the risk of a publicly exposed cloud storage bucket?

options.text: Enforce default-deny public access at the account level
options.rationale: Correct: blocking public access by default prevents accidental exposure.

options.text: Continuously scan configuration for public buckets
options.rationale: Correct: configuration monitoring catches drift that exposes data.
Performance tier is unrelated to access exposure.
Versioning does not restrict who can read the objects.
Renaming does not control access permissions.

items.explanation: Default-deny public access and configuration monitoring address exposure directly.
